Young Martin: They Are Turning This 90s Comedy Into a Gritty Modern Drama

archive // Apr 23, 2026 · Updated Sep 24, 2026

Watch on YouTube

I couldn't believe this was real. They're doing a Young Martin prequel, and here's the catch: they're turning it into an hour-long, gritty drama set in modern-day Detroit.

How do you take the peak physical comedy of the '90s and turn it into a serious drama?

Martin was physical comedy at its peak

Martin ran on Fox from 1992 to 1997, and it was Martin Lawrence at full power. He didn't just play Martin Payne. He also played Sheneneh, Jerome, Mama Payne, Otis the security guard and more, sometimes several of them in the same episode.

The show ran on energy: the falls, the faces, the timing and a studio audience losing it. Martin, Gina, Tommy, Pam and Cole felt like family, and the laugh track was part of the fun. Martin Lawrence's energy had so much soul, and you can't separate it from the format.

What Young Martin is supposed to be

Young Martin was announced in July 2024, with Martin Lawrence producing. It follows a teenage Martin Payne in present-day Detroit, and it's pitched as an hour-long drama about family, friendship and growing up, built around a teenager "characterized by ambition, humor, and a genuine compassion for those around him."

If that sounds familiar, it's because it's the Bel-Air playbook: take a beloved '90s sitcom and re-imagine it as a serious, cinematic drama.

Why the gritty remake keeps missing the point

Bel-Air did it to The Fresh Prince. It changed the tone, the theme and the whole point of the show, and turned a comedy into a prestige drama.

I get why studios do it. The name brings the nostalgia, and drama feels more "premium." But it uses the nostalgia while throwing away the reason people are nostalgic in the first place. Martin worked because it was genuinely funny, loud and silly, with real heart underneath. Take the comedy out, and all that's left is the name.

Modern TV wants to make everything dark and sterile. Not everything needs to be.

Update (September 2026): The Varnell Hill Show got it right

Here's the good news. There's a new Martin spin-off, and it's the opposite of Young Martin.

The Varnell Hill Show premiered on Paramount+ on September 1. Tommy Davidson is back as Varnell Hill, Martin's old rival, in a workplace comedy set behind the scenes of a long-running late-night talk show, where Varnell is fighting to stay relevant in a fast-changing entertainment world. Martin Lawrence has a recurring role, and the cast includes Kym Whitley, Wendy Raquel Robinson, Nick Cafero, Emmanuel Hudson and Chris Williams, with guest stars like Damon Wayans, Mike Epps, Deon Cole, Ms. Pat and Omarion. The eight-episode first season runs weekly through October 13.

And I love it. It's got the laugh track, just like back in the day. They didn't go the modern, cinematic route, and they didn't change what the show is about, the way they did when The Fresh Prince became Bel-Air. It feels like Martin's world, and that's exactly how it should feel.

As for Young Martin, I haven't seen a network or a premiere date announced yet.

Sources: Deadline, The Hollywood Reporter, Variety, Deadline on Young Martin

Quick answers

What is The Varnell Hill Show? A Martin spin-off comedy on Paramount+, starring Tommy Davidson as Varnell Hill and set behind the scenes of a late-night talk show. It premiered September 1, 2026.

Is Martin Lawrence in The Varnell Hill Show? Yes, in a recurring role.

What is Young Martin? A planned hour-long drama prequel about a teenage Martin Payne in present-day Detroit, announced in 2024. It doesn't have a network or premiere date yet.

When did Martin air? On Fox, from 1992 to 1997.

Your turn

Would you watch a gritty Young Martin, or do you want more shows like The Varnell Hill Show? Tell me in the comments.
